column3: The Hebrew has singular collective “Amorite” and “Canaanite,” singular “their heart,” and says that no spirit remained in them.
The Hebrew says “for yourself” and combines “again” with “a second time.”
The Hebrew says “for himself”; the place name literally means “Hill of the Foreskins.”
The Hebrew explicitly includes “the males” and repeats “from Egypt.”
The Hebrew describes the wilderness-born group with an active verb and unspecified agents: they had not circumcised them.
The Hebrew says “the voice of the LORD” and repeats “the LORD” three times.
The Hebrew leaves the subject of raising up the sons unnamed, then explicitly names Joshua as the one who circumcised them. BSB names Joshua as the subject of both actions.
The Hebrew uses an active naming verb with an unnamed singular subject, where BSB uses “has been called.”
The Hebrew narrates camping and observing Passover as coordinated actions rather than making camping a “while” clause.
The Hebrew says they ate that year; BSB adds “began to.”
The Hebrew retains the image of lifting his eyes and explicitly repeats Joshua as he approaches.
The reply begins literally “No”; the Hebrew says Joshua fell on his face to the earth and bowed down.
The Hebrew names Joshua as the addressee and uses singular “sandal” and “foot.”
